grades.question: For a six-inch drainage pipe under the 2022 NYC Plumbing Code, does a cleanout need more than eighteen inches of clearance in front of its face?
grades.expected: No; pipes6in and smaller require at least18in measured perpendicular to the opening face. Exactly18 meets this condition.
grades.answerText: No—where this rule applies, 18 inches is the required minimum, not a requirement to provide more than 18 inches. For sanitary drainage, that distance is measured perpendicular from the cleanout opening’s face to an obstruction (PC § 708.1.9; § 701.1). For storm drainage, the sanitary cleanout provisions apply except for subsurface drainage systems (PC § 1101.8; § 1101.1).

grades.question: The pipe is actually eight inches. We still have eighteen inches in front of the cleanout. Is that sufficient?

grades.answerText: If this is sanitary drainage, or storm drainage that is not a subsurface drainage system, **no**: 18 inches is 18 inches short. For cleanouts on 8-inch-and-larger piping, the 2022 NYC Plumbing Code requires at least 36 inches, measured perpendicular from the opening’s face to an obstruction (PC § 708.1.9; sanitary-drainage scope at § 701.1). Storm cleanouts follow the sanitary cleanout provisions except for a subsurface drainage system (PC § 1101.8; storm-drainage scope at § 1101.1); that exception does not establish that 18 inches is sufficient.
